questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Plane Given Its Cartesian Equation
questions.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $7y-z-13=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨0,7,-1⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}7y-z-13 & =0 \\ z & =7y-13.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $y=0$, we get $z=-13.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,-13)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,-13⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,-13⟩)\cdot ⟨0,7,-1⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}5y-z+17 & =0 \\ z & =5y+17.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $y=0$, we get $z=17.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,17)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,17⟩.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Vector
questions.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(2,1,-5)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨6,-2,0⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨2,1,-5⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨6,-2,0⟩.$

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨6,-2,0⟩ & =⟨2,1,-5⟩\cdot ⟨6,-2,0⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨6,-2,0⟩ & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨6,-2,0⟩ & =10 \\ 6x-2y & =10 \\ 6x-2y-10 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Vectors
questions.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨-4,3,5⟩.$

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -6\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & -3 & -6 \\ 0 & 2 & -8\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =36i+16j+4k \\  & =⟨36,16,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨36,16,4⟩ & =⟨-4,3,5⟩\cdot ⟨36,16,4⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨36,16,4⟩ & =-76\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨36,16,4⟩ & =-76 \\ 36x+16y+4z & =-76 \\ 36x+16y+4z+76 & =0 \\ 9x+4y+z+19 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Line
questions.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(2,-3,1)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
$r=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨2,-3,1⟩.$ From the vectorial equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨4,0,-2⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is

$$
n=⟨4,0,-2⟩,
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨4,0,-2⟩ & =⟨2,-3,1⟩\cdot ⟨4,0,-2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨4,0,-2⟩ & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute  $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨4,0,-2⟩ & =3 \\ 4x-2z & =6 \\ 4x-2z-6 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
